Salient Features

 
BRIEF RESUME OF THE WORK DONE DURING THE PERIOD UNDER REVIEW
PRIORITY AREA-I: RESEARCH
                        The All India Coordinated Research Project on Spices is an important landmark in the history of spice crops. It provided a major and important plateform for placing spice research in the country on a sound footing. Its multi-disciplinary approach has been playing an important role in generating region specific technology. I am working in All India Coordinated Research Project on Spices ever since my appointment in the विश्वविद्यालय.
कार्यों का प्रकार involved
  • Planning of research experiments of the scheme
  • Procurement/preparation of material for experimentation
  • Conducting various experiments of the project
  • Processing of research data and writing research articles
  • Preparation and presentation of technical reports of the scheme
  • Managing financial requirements of the scheme
  • Crop demonstration and trainings to popularize the spices and technologies generated
Salient features of research work:
  • Collection, evaluation and maintenance of germplasm of seed spices for developing high yielding/improved varieties
  • Testing of promising selections/recommended varieties under multi-location trials
  • Standardization of agro-techniques to achieve higher yield
  • Demonstration of technology/varieties developed at farmer’s field

  • Maximum response of biofertilizers (Azotobacter/Azospirillum) in coriander was observed at medium fertility level. However, seed treated with Azotobacter and supplied with 50% of the recommended nitrogen significantly improved growth and seed yield.
  •  Azotobacter strain Msx-9 was found most effective for improving growth and seed yield in fennel and coriander.
  • Three irrigation ( based on 75mm CPE) at branching, flowering and seed filling stage along with 60 kg N/ha and 40 kg P2O5/ha at a spacing of 30 x 20 cm has been recommended for raising a successful seed crop of coriander in Haryana . 
  • Maximum leaf yield of coriander was recorded with two cuttings in variety DH-228 (192.0q/ha) followed by DH-266 (188.8 q/ha).  There was no significant reduction in seed yield when two leaf cuttings were taken in variety DH-228. 
  • In coriander, for green leaf cutting 90 kg N/ha has been recommended for obtaining higher leaf yield in variety Hisar Bhoomit (DH-228).
  • In coriander, the maximum seed yield was recorded with the application of zinc sulphate @ 20 kg/ha as soil application which was statistically at par with ferrous sulphate @ 5 kg/ha soil application + 0.125% as foliar application.
  • Effect of inorganic nitrogen, FYM and bio-fertilizers in coriander revealed that maximum seed yield was recorded in inorganic nitrogen (100%) + Azospirillum @ 1.5 kg/ha +5t FYM/ha and inorganic nitrogen (100%) alone which was statistically at par with inorganic nitrogen (75%) + Azospirillum @ 1.5 kg/ha +5t FYM/ha.
  • In coriander, among bio-regulators, maximum seed yield was recorded with the application of NAA @ 50 ppm when three sprays were given followed by two sprays.
  • For production of leafy type coriander in off season (summer), among the three shade levels, 50% shade resulted in higher leaf yield (10312Kg/ha) followed by 75% shade. Among the entries tested, DH-228 (9990 Kg/ha) produced maximum leaf yield under all the shading nets followed by DH- 259 (9011 Kg/ha).
  • In experiment on nutrient supplementation through organic manures for growth and yield of coriander, the maximum seed yield was recorded with the application of 100% nitrogen supplemented with vermicompost (2138 kg/ha) followed by nitrogen supplemented with FYM 25% + vermicompost 75% (1928 kg/ha).
  • The optimum time of coriander crop under Haryana condition was 1st November  and  application of 75 kg N/ha and foliar spray of  GA3 @ 25 ppm at 40 days after sowing resulted in higher leafy yield.
  • Sowing time of fenugreek under Hisar conditions extends from mid September to mid January with yield reduced to half at last sowing. The optimum time of sowing in fenugreek cv. Hisar Sonali was 1st week of November at spacing of 30 x 10 cm.
  • In fenugreek, the pre-emergence application of pendimethalin @ 0.75kg/ha supplemented with one hand weeding at 45 days after sowing was found most effective in controlling weeds and increasing seed yield.
  • In Ajowain, maximum seed yield was recorded when sowing was done on 20th October at the spacing of 30 x 20 cm.
  • The seed rate and spacing trial in ajowain revealed that maximum seed yield was obtained with 2.5 kg/ha seed at a spacing of 30x20 cm.
  • Application of gibberellic acid@ 100ppm at juvenile stage for obtaining higher yield of Ajowain is recommended.
  • In coriander, the maximum seed yield was observed with the application of Rhizobacteria FL-18 (seed treatment + soil application) followed by Trichoderma MTCC- 5179 at experimental field as well as under large scale demonstration at farmer’s field.
  • In fenugreek, maximum seed yield was recorded with the application of Rhizobacteria FK 14+FL 18 (Seed + Soil treatment) followed by  Trichoderma MTCC- 5179  at experimental field as well as under large scale demonstration at farmer’s field.
  •  In fennel, the maximum seed yield was found with the application of Trichoderma MTCC-5179 followed by Rhizobacteria FL-14 (seed treatment) at experimental field as well as under large scale demonstration at farmer’s field.
  • In fennel, seed quality decreases with the increasing umbel order. Seeds from main and primary umbels are vigorous and better in performance than secondary and tertiary order umbels.
  • In garlic, maximum bulb yield was recorded with application of 50 kg N/ha with sowing at a spacing of 15x10 cm.
  • In carrot, higher yield of quality roots with least forking was recorded when sowing was done on 30th September with line sowing of seeds on ridges.
  • In carrot, maximum root yield was obtained with application of oxyfluorfen 100 g/ha integrated with one hoeing at 40 DAS  which was statistically at par with  oxadiagyl 100 g/ha + HW, pendimethalin 1.0 Kg/ha+ HW and weed free treatment.
  • The epidemiological studies on stem gall of coriander revealed that the early sown crop (Oct.) has more disease intensity as compared to late sown crop. It was also observed that the disease appeared only in DH-5 and DH-36 (seed type varieties) while DH-228 and DH-266 (leafy type) were free from the disease.

            D. PLANT PROTECTION :
  1. Population dynamics of coriander aphid was studied on ten different cultivars/varieties during 2002-03 and 2003-04. The peak incidence of the pest was recorded during the end of February and 1st week of March (av.31.5 aphids/umbel). On the basis of season’s average cv. JCO-283 was found to be the most susceptible and cv. DH-246, the least susceptible.
  2. In coriander during 2005-06 and 2006-07, cultivar NDC-2 was observed to be least susceptible to aphids (10.2 aphids / umbel) followed by JCO-328 (18.6 aphids / umbel) while in fenugreek cultivar HM-65 was observed to be least susceptible.
  3. The epidemiological studies on stem gall of coriander revealed that the early sown crop (16th Oct.) has more disease intensity as compared to late sown crop (10th Nov.). It was also observed that the disease appeared only in DH-5 and DH-36 (seed type varieties) while DH-228 and DH-266 (leafy type) were free from the disease. 
  4. The response of coriander aphid (Hyadaphis coriandri) on different genotypes of coriander was recorded during ‘rabi’ season of 2008-09. The coriander aphid started appearing on the crop in the third week of February and reached to its peak in the second week of March and maximum population was observed on Gujarat Coriander-1. Among twenty genotypes screened, none was completely free from infestation. On the basis of season’s average Gujarat Coriander-1 harboured maximum population (27.72 aphids/umbel) while Hisar Bhoomit, Swathi, CS-6, Sindhu, RCr-436, Jawahar Dhania-1, Hisar Sugandh and Hisar Anand had relatively low infestation of H. coriandri (0.73 to 1.08 aphids/umbel).
